RULES.topic: Voter ID requirements at the polls (SB 276)
RULES.currentRule: Effective for 2026: acceptable primary ID is a Montana driver's license, Montana state ID card, tribal photo ID, military ID card, U.S. passport, Montana concealed-carry permit, or a student photo ID issued by a Montana University System school or an NCAA-member school. If a voter's ID is not on this primary list (e.g., a non-NCAA-affiliated student ID), the voter must also present a secondary document showing name and current address (utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, vehicle registration, or other government document). SB 276 tightened the prior rule, under which any photo ID was sufficient on its own.
RULES.whyItMatters: MT-01 voters across all 16 counties should bring a primary-list photo ID; those relying on a non-qualifying student ID must also carry a secondary proof-of-address document. If ID is insufficient or the voter's name isn't in the precinct register, the voter may sign the register and cast a provisional ballot (Montana uses signature verification for provisional ballots).
RULES.detail: SB 276 was challenged in the same lawsuit as SB 490 but was NOT blocked by the May 11, 2026 court order; SB 276's ID rules remain in effect for the 2026 general election.

RULES.topic: Absentee envelope-return requirements, including new birth-year mandate
RULES.currentRule: Voters must (1) place the voted ballot in the secrecy envelope, (2) place the secrecy envelope inside the return signature envelope, and (3) sign, date, and write their birth year in the dedicated space on the return envelope. The person to whom the ballot was issued must be the one who signs the return envelope. The birth-year requirement is new for 2026 (first applied in 2025 municipal elections, then 2026 school elections).
RULES.whyItMatters: MT-01 voters returning an absentee ballot must complete all three steps, including the new birth-year field, or risk having their ballot flagged as rejected. As of the May 2026 primary, roughly 0.25% of ballots statewide were in rejected status.
RULES.detail: Gallatin County requires a wet-ink (non-digital) signature on any rejection-resolution or replacement-ballot form, per the county's Election Forms page.

RULES.topic: Ballot status tracking and rejection resolution
RULES.currentRule: Voters can track ballot status (SENT / RECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED) via VoteMT.gov and resolve a rejected ballot (missing/incorrect signature or missing/incorrect birth year) at votemt.gov/resolve-my-ballot/.
RULES.whyItMatters: MT-01 voters whose absentee ballot is flagged as rejected have a defined path to cure the defect and ensure their vote counts; Gallatin County specifically requires a wet-ink signature on the cure/replacement form.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: exact cure-window length (how many days after Election Day a voter has to cure a rejected ballot) was not independently confirmed on a primary source in this research pass.

RULES.topic: SB 490 (Saturday-before-election hours / Election Day registration cutoff) — enjoined
RULES.currentRule: SB 490 (signed May 5, 2025) would have (1) ended federal-election Election Day registration at noon instead of 8:00 PM, (2) ended late registration on the Monday before Election Day at noon instead of continuing, and (3) required county election offices to open the Saturday before Election Day for expanded registration/voting. On May 11, 2026, Judge Adam Larsen (Montana First Judicial District Court, Lewis and Clark County) issued a preliminary injunction blocking all SB 490 provisions statewide as 'likely unconstitutional under the Montana Constitution.'
RULES.whyItMatters: For the November 3, 2026 general election, MT-01 voters retain Election Day registration until 8:00 PM (not noon), the Monday-before-election cutoff remains noon (unchanged), and county offices are NOT required to open the Saturday before the election. This is a preliminary injunction, not a final ruling — litigation remains ongoing and could change the rule again before or after Nov. 3, 2026.
RULES.detail: Plaintiffs: seven Montana Indian tribes, Western Native Voice, ACLU of Montana, Forward Montana, Montana Public Interest Research Group, Montana Federation of Public Employees. Defendant: Secretary of State Christi Jacobsen; intervenors: RNC and Montana GOP. NEEDS REVIEW closer to Election Day for any updated ruling.

RULES.topic: Registration-deadline framing discrepancy between EAC and VoteMT.gov
RULES.currentRule: The U.S. EAC's Montana Profile (Jan. 2026) describes Montana's 'registration deadline' as 'noon the day before Election Day' — this appears to describe the late-registration in-person cutoff pattern, not the 30-day regular-registration close. VoteMT.gov's own calendar and FAQ distinguish 'regular registration close' (Oct. 5, 2026, 5:00 PM) from 'late registration' (Oct. 6, 2026 through Election Day, in-person only).
RULES.whyItMatters: Dashboard users should be pointed to the more precise VoteMT.gov framing (Oct. 5 regular close vs. Oct. 6-Nov. 3 late/in-person registration) rather than the EAC's single 'noon the day before' framing, to avoid confusion about the true regular-registration deadline.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: this is a source-framing conflict, not a legal dispute; see CONFLICTS below.

CONFLICTS.factInQuestion: Whether Montana's 'voter registration deadline' is most accurately described as a single noon-before-Election-Day cutoff or as two distinct phases (regular close vs. late/in-person registration).
CONFLICTS.sourceAClaim: VoteMT.gov's official voter calendar and FAQ distinguish a 'regular registration close' on October 5, 2026 at 5:00 PM (online/mail/in-person) from a separate 'late registration' period from October 6, 2026 through Election Day (in-person only, ballot obtained in person).
CONFLICTS.sourceBClaim: The U.S. EAC's Montana Profile (Jan. 2026) describes Montana's registration deadline in a single line as 'noon the day before Election Day,' without distinguishing the two-phase structure.
CONFLICTS.whyItMatters: MT-01 voters need a single, clear registration-deadline framing. Using only the EAC's single-line description could cause a voter who could still register in person through Election Day to mistakenly believe registration closed weeks earlier.
CONFLICTS.suggestedReviewAction: Use VoteMT.gov's two-phase framing (regular close Oct. 5, late/in-person Oct. 6-Nov. 3) as the authoritative dashboard framing; cite the EAC profile only as secondary context, not as the primary deadline statement.

CONFLICTS.factInQuestion: Final ballot-qualification status of independent candidate Kimberly Persico for the MT-01 general election.
CONFLICTS.sourceAClaim: As of May 26, 2026 (the filing deadline), Persico had only 562 accepted signatures against a required 6,742 (4% of Zinke's 2024 winning vote total) — far short of the threshold.
CONFLICTS.sourceBClaim: Montana Free Press's confirmed general-election field framing treats Flint (R), Forstag (D), and Sheedy (L) as the settled ballot, with Persico's status described as pending/unlikely rather than finally resolved.
CONFLICTS.whyItMatters: The Secretary of State's final independent/minor-party certification deadline (August 20, 2026) falls after this report's compilation date. Publishing Persico as either 'on the ballot' or 'not on the ballot' before that date risks being wrong in either direction.
CONFLICTS.suggestedReviewAction: Mark Persico's status as 'likely not qualifying, unconfirmed' and re-check sosmt.gov's certification announcement after August 20, 2026 before finalizing the general-election candidate list.
